overall: The AG found the Brookline School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by listing an insufficiently specific topic on its October 10, 2024 notice, declined to nullify the October 10 vote, and found no intentional violation; it ordered future compliance only.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Oct. 10 notice topic '2025-2026 School Calendar (2nd Reading and Possible Vote)' did not disclose that the committee would discuss designating Eid al-Fitr as a Category I holiday.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notice topic “2025-2026 School Calendar (2nd Reading and Possible Vote)” was insufficient to inform the public of the reasonably anticipated nature of the October 10 discussion—the designation of Eid al-Fitr as a Category I holiday and the district’s approach to holidays more broadly.

allegations.summary: Complaint asked that the committee's October 10 vote designating Eid al-Fitr as a Category I holiday be nullified as the remedy for the notice violation.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons we decline to nullify the Committee’s October 10 vote.

allegations.summary: On request for further review, complainant asserted the notice violation was intentional, citing the committee's anticipation of the topic and a member's warning during the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not find that the Committee acted to intentionally violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
